classification.analysis: Starmer resigned June 22 after catastrophic May local elections saw Labour lose 1,500 councillors and 35 councils. Reform UK now leads polls at 26%, nearly double their 2024 result, while Labour collapsed from 34% to under 20%. Andy Burnham expected to succeed as PM. Party in crisis mode.

Merz's grand coalition is collapsing after just over a year. AfD now leads all polls at 28%, while the CDU/CSU-SPD coalition has plummeted to 34.6% from 44.9% at election. With 71% disapproval and only 15% satisfaction, Merz faces internal disputes over key policies. Consumer confidence remains deeply negative amid economic stagnation and energy concerns.

Macron's approval hit historic low of 18% in April 2026 amid rising unemployment (8.1%, highest in 5 years) and political instability. Far-right RN dominates 2027 election polling at 31-37%, more than double any centrist alternative. Budget passed in February only after four-month deadlock and failed no-confidence votes, exposing government fragility.

Sánchez governs precariously after Junts withdrew support in October 2025, though opposition cannot muster no-confidence motion. May 2026 Andalusian election delivered PSOE's worst-ever regional result. Multiple corruption scandals involving his wife, brother, and senior party officials compound political pressure. Vox rising but PP remains leading opposition force.

After March 2026's historic election defeat—Social Democrats' worst result since 1903—Frederiksen spent over two months in caretaker limbo before forming a fragile minority government on June 1. The far-right Danish People's Party has tripled its vote share and now leads the blue bloc at 11%, while the new coalition commands just 46% versus 53% at the 2022 election. Immediate challenge: navigating Trump's Greenland crisis.

One Nation's surge to 29-30% has overtaken Labor at 27% in June polling, a dramatic reversal from the May 2025 election when Labor won 34.7% to One Nation's 6.2%. The government's May budget flopped badly, and One Nation's 'Fire The Liar' fundraiser raised $4 million targeting Albanese. Despite a landmark $2.5 billion defence export to Canada, consumer confidence remains stuck near 80, well below the neutral 100 level.

Martin faces mounting internal pressure to resign after Ireland's EU presidency ends, with a majority of Fianna Fáil parliamentarians favoring leadership change. The coalition was punished over an energy crisis in May, with consumer confidence declining from year-ago levels. Recent by-election defeats for Sinn Féin have paradoxically complicated coalition calculations as Social Democrats emerge as potential kingmakers. Housing crisis remains politically charged.

Jetten's minority coalition faces mounting pressure as consumer confidence plummets to -46, the weakest since January 2023. In April, the Senate rejected his asylum bill, prompting accusations of PVV sabotage. Coalition polling has dropped 6.5 points since the October election, though the fractured far-right remains contained at 13.5%. The housing crisis and healthcare cuts test his centrist mandate.

Montenegro's minority government faces mounting pressure after a nationwide general strike paralyzed Portugal on June 3 over controversial labor reforms. Polling shows the coalition collapsing from 32% to 23.7%, now trailing the opposition PS. The government increasingly relies on far-right Chega's support for key legislation, including transgender restrictions approved in March, marking deepening political fragmentation.

Støre faces severe polling erosion just ten months after re-election. Progress Party now leads at 31% versus Labour's 22%, a dramatic reversal. Government signed major defence pact with France including nuclear deterrence cooperation, while tightening immigration policy and providing substantial military aid to Ukraine amid rising far-right consolidation.

Takaichi's historic February landslide delivered a two-thirds supermajority, but her honeymoon is fading fast. Cabinet approval has plummeted from 69% in February to 51% by late June, hammered by a defamatory video scandal and parliamentary stonewalling allegations. Party support languishes in the 20s despite the coalition's dominance. Far-right Sanseito quintupled its seats to 15 but remains marginal at 3%.

Michal's coalition has collapsed from 53.8% to 27.9% in polls since the 2023 election, with Reform down to 11.8%. Consumer confidence remains deeply negative at -32.5. Recent focus on Ukraine support and Nordic-Baltic cooperation. Coalition faces likely defeat to conservative Isamaa (26.3%) in 2027, though far-right EKRE remains contained at 13.5%.

Kristersson's coalition trails badly at 43.8% ahead of September election, down from 50.4% in 2022. Sweden Democrats now dominate the right bloc at 19.4%, overtaking Moderates at 17.2%. March agreement promised SD cabinet posts if coalition wins. Senior Moderates reportedly want Kristersson replaced. Government making desperate last-minute tax cut promises to families.

Orpo's coalition faces severe pressure with opposition filing no-confidence motion over poverty and youth unemployment hitting 28%. Government support has collapsed from 48.8% at election to just 38.3%, while SDP leads polls at 23.9%. Consumer confidence deteriorated to -8.7, lowest since early 2025. Finns Party remains in government despite losing a third of its 2023 support.

Mitsotakis faces mounting pressure as New Democracy polling drops 11 points since 2023 while Greek Solution gains modestly. June consumer confidence hit -46.9, worst in EU. Despite EU praise for removing Greece from macroeconomic imbalance list, the OPEKEPE farm subsidy scandal damaged credibility. Opposition fragmentation with Tsipras launching new ELAS party creates political instability ahead of 2027 election.

Stocker's three-party coalition faces severe internal divisions over EU directives, paralyzing legislation. FPÖ dominates polls at 37%, up 8 points since the election, while the coalition has collapsed to 46%, teetering on the edge of losing its majority. Budget disputes and coalition infighting define Austria's political landscape.

De Wever's Arizona coalition maintains solid parliamentary support at 57.3% of seats despite implementing deeply unpopular austerity measures including VAT hikes and pension reforms. Consumer confidence has improved from -12.9 to -7 over the past year. Vlaams Belang remains excluded by cordon sanitaire despite polling at 16%, while national strikes signal rising discontent with spending cuts.

Luxon's coalition has collapsed from 53% to 49% since 2023, with National hemorrhaging support while NZ First doubles its vote share. Late-June scandals over emergency housing targets and rough sleepers revealed acute policy failures. Consumer confidence crashed to 80.4, lowest since 2023. Leadership speculation intensified after disastrous polling, with the November election looming and the coalition barely clinging to majority.

Meloni's far-right government faces mounting pressures after nearly four years. A constitutional referendum defeat forced ministerial resignations, while the coalition has lost its parliamentary majority in polls, dropping to 42.3% from 44% at election. Consumer confidence fell nearly 4 points year-over-year. A stunning public rift with Trump and controversial school censorship laws mark institutional stress. Meloni now considers early elections, worried about sliding approval.

Babiš's ANO-SPD-Motorists coalition faces mounting resistance seven months into power. A massive 250,000-person protest in March opposed democratic erosion. The coalition pushed controversial referendum thresholds requiring supermajority approval they lack by 12 votes. Consumer confidence dropped from 110.4 to 103.4 year-over-year. Coalition polling declined from 49.1% at election to 44.8% currently, reflecting early institutional consolidation meeting fierce public pushback.

Trump's approval has collapsed to 39.4% from 47% at inauguration, driven by tariff-induced inflation hitting 4.5%. Consumer sentiment reached historic lows in May before modest June recovery. Independent approval at 34% signals potential Democratic wave in 2026 midterms. Economic anxiety dominates as cost-of-living pressures mount.

Magyar's Tisza won a supermajority in April 2026, ousting Orbán after 16 years. Just two months in, polling shows Tisza at 67%. However, his constitutional amendment to remove President Sulyok has drawn criticism from Fidesz and international observers, with the Venice Commission reviewing the conflict. The amendment passed June 15, imposing term limits and enabling removal of Orbán-era appointees.

Fico's coalition has collapsed from 43% to 29% support as institutional dismantling accelerates. His son's alleged €100,000 party payments sparked corruption allegations. Consumer confidence hit three-year lows amid economic pressure. Republika at 11% represents far-right fragmentation. Progressive Slovakia leads polls at 20%, positioning as democratic alternative.

Milei's Cabinet chief Adorni resigned June 28 amid corruption scandal, undermining his anti-graft platform. Approval collapsed from 53% at inauguration to 40%, hitting 35% in April. Real wages down 9% despite inflation falling to 30%. Opposition fragmented but Peronists consolidating around Kicillof and Kirchner.

Netanyahu's coalition collapsed in late June after ultra-Orthodox parties withdrew over draft legislation, leaving him with 50-52 seats versus 58 for the opposition. Former IDF chief Eisenkot has emerged as the leading challenger ahead of October elections. The far-right coalition faces near-certain defeat after 3.5 years marked by judicial overhaul attempts and October 7 failures.

Erdoğan intensified authoritarian crackdown in June 2026, with Istanbul Mayor İmamoğlu jailed facing 2,000-year sentence and opposition CHP headquarters raided. Inflammatory rhetoric escalated as he declared Israeli strikes 'threaten Turkey.' Economic distress persists despite slight consumer confidence uptick. Systematic judicial capture eliminates credible opposition challengers ahead of 2028 election, consolidating one-man rule through institutional destruction.

Tusk's coalition has lost its majority in polls, dropping from 53.7% to 46.4% as Third Way collapses internally. President Nawrocki blocks key reforms including EU arms credits Tusk called 'treason.' June hospital corruption scandal further damaged credibility. Confederation doubled to 13.7% but remains secondary to PiS's 26.5%. Coalition fragmentation threatens governing capacity ahead of 2027 election.

Carney maintains commanding polling leads fifteen months into office, launching major AI and food security strategies in June. However, he conceded on June 30 that emissions targets will be missed, a politically risky move that signals growing economic pressures despite strong government approval ratings and continued Liberal dominance across key regions.

Lee's approval fell below 50% for first time, dropping to 46.5% after six consecutive weekly declines. Ballot shortage controversy from June 3 local elections and economic distrust drive discontent. Consumer confidence slipped from 108.7 to 106.6 year-over-year. Democratic Party tied with opposition at 41-42%. Recent G7 trip focused on North Korea diplomacy amid mounting governance pressures.

Sheinbaum faces mounting challenges 21 months into her transformational presidency. Her approval has declined from 70% at inauguration amid corruption and crime concerns. In early June 2026, she delivered an aggressive sovereignty speech pushing back against US pressure on trade and security matters. The OECD slashed Mexico's 2026 growth forecast to 0.8%, while teacher protests threaten World Cup disruptions.
